summary: Tested event card order and age info, home event strip, the upcoming-only events API, and the Male/Female gender options on the profile page. Everything requested passed in the backend (5/5 pytest) and frontend (Playwright, EN and FR). Did not press Refresh events and did not test Stripe or AI preview.

issues: Brumelance genre line reads 'Immersive adult LARP (Brumelance), 18+'. It repeats the age, which the ai.py prompt says to keep out of the genre.
In FR, the location text is still in English (e.g. 'between Victoriaville and Drummondville ... venue for this date not confirmed'). Location is a single field with no location_fr.
Home strip cards have different widths because they only set min-w (the Bicolline card is much wider). The MapPin icon is not lined up when the location wraps to several lines.
Age, date and recurrence texts are long AI sentences, so the cards are tall. Consider asking for a short age_range (e.g. '18+') plus an optional note.

action_items: Optional: strip age info out of genre_en/genre_fr, or tighten the prompt.
Optional: add location_fr, or ask for locations without English notes.
Optional: give home event strip cards a fixed width (e.g. w-[260px] shrink-0).
critical_code_review_comments: Profile.jsx stores non-binary as the value 'non-binary person'. It works, but it is an odd stored value; 'non-binary' would be cleaner if the AI prompt does not depend on it.
list_events compares ISO date strings against today in UTC. In the evening Montreal time, an event happening today will drop off the list early.
seed_data_creation: Guest profiles were created for random uuid4 X-Guest-Ids (one from pytest, one from the browser). There is no delete endpoint, so they were not removed.
context_for_next_testing_agent: 3 events in DB (Brumelance 2026-11-21, Bicolline 2026-11-21 recurring, Festival des GN 2027-02-06), all with age_range_en/fr. Card DOM order checked: name(a, target=_blank) > genre > age > location > datetime > recurrence. No 'Source' link and no 'not listed' text. Gender options checked in EN and FR; female persists through the API and after reload.
